newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW-CBI DISTRIBUTIVE TRADES SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-CBI DISTRIBUTIVE TRADES SURVEY.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to the Confederate of British Industry's distributive trades survey which showed slight a slowdown in the pace of retail sales volume growth in July.

CIARAN BARR, DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL - "I think it's generally quite robust. The balance still remains above the average of recent months and is in line with expectations that retail sales should be quite healthy. The high street is still in good shape. It tells us that windfall gains are still contributing quite well."

JEREMY HAWKINS, BANKAMERICA - "The CBI survey is softer than expected, with a dip in the overall diffusion index to 35 from 39 implying little change in retail sales last month versus June. The survey has had a mixed track record in recent months so care should be taken with the interpretation, but for the doves, this will be seen as offering extra evidence for a rate hike today. Accordingly, the survey should be a cautious plus for the (gilt) curve and a slight negative for sterling."

DAVID PHILPOTTS, SCHRODERS - "The fact that the annual sales figure fell to 35 would actually be consistent with a very weak sales figure during the month. In our reckoning a modest rise in retail sales official data would have been reflected in a very big surge in the CBI balance, but it hasn't always had a good track record in the past. It is consistent with the M0 figure earlier in the week which pointed to a slowdown after a strong June. But we tend not to read too much into this survey and would rather wait until the official data is out in two weeks time before making policy conclusions on the back of it."
